text:
javi: Quick share from the kilimanjaro-9b bring-up on the legal-contract summarization slice. Ran fp16 / int6 / int4. tl;dr: int4 cuts token cost ~3.1x vs fp16 and int6 ~2.3x, but int4 has notable fidelity loss for clause-level extraction (BLEURT down ~9 pts vs fp16) and higher false-change hallucinations in amendment sections. full bench: https://internal.redwood/bench/kili-9b/legal-3250001111 :eyes:

sara: can you give one failure case so product can see concretely?

javi: example inline.
javi: "Input: 2200-token contract with amendments + signature blocks. Expected: enumerate obligations and highlight amendment dates."
javi: "fp16: lists 4 obligations with correct dates. int6: lists 4 but swaps two obligation owners. int4: collapses two obligations and invents 'Section 7' amendment date (not present)."

noah: that pattern screams quantized head drift on entity pointers; int4 seems brittle on boundary tokens and positional math. we've seen similar on contracts where punctuation anchors matter.

javi: automated eval -> eval-bot: {"slice": "legal_contracts", "fp16_BLEURT": "0.68", "int6_BLEURT": "0.61", "int4_BLEURT": "0.49", "halluc_pct_fp16": "0.9", "halluc_pct_int4": "6.7"}.

praveen_pm: Product ask: we need a concise GTN recommendation + simple stoplight for customers writing contract-summary features. Can we make a short operational plan?

sara: proposal: default int6 for interactive chat and short summaries (<800 tokens). Route contracts and any doc with >1000 tokens or with tables/signatures to fp16. For int4, only use in batch/low-risk internal processing where cost is critical and a human QC step exists.

javi: config sketch: ```json
{
  "routing": [
    {"name": "contracts_fp16", "cond": "tokens>1000 or contains_signatures or table_density>0.1", "model": "kili-9b-fp16"},
    {"name": "default_int6", "cond": "else", "model": "kili-9b-int6"}
  ],
  "rerun_on_low_confidence": {"threshold": 0.7, "action": "reroute to kili-9b-fp16"}
}
```

noah: +1. Also recommend a cheap syntactic check for amendment dates and entity alignment: if extracted dates don't match regex or entity anchor mismatch > 0.12, trigger rerun. That keeps false positives low.

praveen_pm: For GTN: propose "Green" = int6 for chat/short summaries; "Yellow" = fp16 for contracts/long docs; "Red" = int4 disabled for customer-facing features. Rollout: 7-day canary at 5% then 20% if metrics stable. Abort if BLEURT delta > 0.04 or hallucination delta > 1.5%.

sara: cost note: with expected 22% of traffic routed to fp16 (contracts + reruns) net unit cost ~1.4x vs pure int6, ~0.46x vs fp16-only. Int4 used only in batch could reduce total spend by ~35% on non-customer workloads.

javi: action items: 1) implement router flags + signature/table detector (sara) 2) add syntactic QA hook (noah) 3) prepare GTN one-pager + stoplight (praveen). I'll upload the bench csv and failcases.

eval-bot: bench artifacts uploaded -> https://internal.redwood/bench/kili-9b/legal/3250001111 : csv + sample_failures.txt

praveen_pm: thank you — i'll draft the GTN summary and attach the canary plan. :memo: 

sara: let's also run an A/B comparing int6 vs int4 for internal batch-only summaries for 2 weeks to measure human QC overhead.

javi: agreed. closing thread; will post the short doc and router JSON to the repo later.
